The '''[[1952 in association football|1952]]–[[1953 in association football|53]] season''' was the 54th completed season of [[The Football League]].

==Final league tables==

The tables below are reproduced here in the exact form that they can be found at [https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1952-53.html The Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation] website<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1952-53.html |title=England 1952-53 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=2010-02-24}}</ref> and in ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79'',<ref name="Rothmans">Ian Laschke: ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79''. Macdonald and Jane’s, London & Sydney, 1980.</ref> with home and away statistics separated.

Beginning with the season 1894–95, clubs finishing level on points were separated according to goal average (goals scored divided by goals conceded), or more properly put, goal ratio. In case one or more teams had the same goal difference, this system favoured those teams who had scored fewer goals. The goal average system was eventually scrapped beginning with the 1976–77 season.

From the 1922–23 season, the bottom two teams of both Third Division North and Third Division South were required to apply for [[re-election (Football League)|re-election]].<ref name=" Rothmans"/>

[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] won their second league title of the postwar era, finishing ahead of runners-up [[Preston North End]] on goal average - denying them a first league title since they won the first two English Football League titles more than 60 years earlier. Preston defeated Arsenal in a 2-0 home win in the second last match of the season on 25 April, which was followed by another win at Derby four days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/preston-north-end/tab/matches/season/1953/ |title=Preston North End club match record 1953 |publisher=11v11.com }}</ref> But Arsenal's 3-2 win in their final match against [[Burnley FC|Burnley]] on 1 May meant that it was Arsenal who clinched the title on goal average.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/arsenal/tab/matches/season/1953/ |title=Arsenal football club match record 1953 |publisher=11v11. com}}</ref>

[[Wolverhampton Wanderers]] bounced back after two disappointing seasons to finish third, three points short of the title. They finished one point ahead of their local rivals [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]]. Twelve goals were scored when [[Blackpool FC|Blackpool]] defeated [[Charlton Athletic]] 8-4 on 25 September, but Charlton would eventually finish two places higher in the table at fifth place. Defending champions [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], in a period of transition as the team captained by [[Johnny Carey]] started to make way for a younger generation of players,{{citation needed|date=September 2020}} finished eighth. 

[[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] and [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]], who had been among the First Division's leading lights in the first few postwar seasons, went down to the Second Division after several seasons of gradually declining form.{{citation needed|date=September 2020}} [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], the 1947 champions, avoided the drop by just two points.

==Second Division==
{{Infobox football league season
| competition        = [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]]
| season             = 1952–53
| winners            = [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]]
| promoted           = [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]]<br />[[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]]
| relegated          = [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]]<br />[[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]]
| league topscorer   = [[Arthur Rowley]]<br />(39 goals)<ref name = "topscorers"/>
| biggest home win   = 
| biggest away win   =

[[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] were champions of the Second Division, scoring 97 goals in the process. Their season included two runs of eleven league matches in a row without defeat, in October-December and February-April respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/sheffield-united/tab/matches/season/1953/ |title=Sheffield United football club match record 1953 |publisher=11v11.com }}</ref>

[[Huddersfield Town F.C|Huddersfield Town]] finished second, two points behind and were promoted to the First Division. [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] were contenders for promotion, but a poor finish without a win in their last four games left them six points behind Huddersfield in third place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/luton-town/tab/matches/season/1953/ |title=Luton Town football club match record 1953 |publisher= 11v11.com }}</ref>

[[Everton F. C.|Everton]] recorded their lowest ever league position, finishing 16th in an uneven season that included a 7-1 victory over [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster]] and a 8-2 defeat against Huddersfield.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/everton/tab/matches/season/1953/ |title=Everton football club match record 1953 |publisher=11v11.com }}</ref>

[[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] were relegated along with [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]], who finished bottom after a poor season that included just five wins, 108 conceded goals and a late run of nine consecutive defeats.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/barnsley/tab/matches/season/1953/ |title=Barnsley football club match record 1953 |publisher=11v11.com }}</ref>
